Summary

Implements admin-controlled user onboarding with magic-link invitations and a self-service waitlist, preparing the app for production OAuth (#276).

- **`AllowedEmail` model** — single model with `status` field (`approved` / `waitlisted`); schema migration + data migration grandfathering all existing users so production accounts keep working when the gate is enabled
- **Allowlist gate** — `auth_google` and `auth_register` check the allowlist before any other logic; dev bypasses only on a fresh DB (first account auto-approved), enforces normally once any user exists; case-insensitive match; returns `{"detail": "...", "code": "not_invited"}` on deny
- **`POST /api/auth/admin-invite/`** (admin only) — upserts `AllowedEmail` to `approved`, generates a 7-day signed token via `django.core.signing`, sends an invitation email, returns 204
- **`POST /api/auth/accept-invite/`** (anonymous) — validates token, returns the email for UI prefill; idempotent, no DB write
- **`POST /api/auth/waitlist/`** (anonymous) — self-service; never demotes an `approved` row
- **`AllowedEmailAdmin`** — list display, filters, two admin actions ("Send invitation email" re-sends to approved rows too for lost-link recovery; "Approve without emailing"); waitlisted rows sort to the top
- **Email delivery** — Django built-in SMTP; production uses Resend via env vars; dev defaults to console backend (invite URL logged as a single copyable line); Mailpit available via `docker compose --profile mail up -d mailpit`
- **Frontend** — "Request Access" button replaces Sign Up; submits waitlist in one click (inline error if email blank); after a `not_invited` auth error (Google or email) the same button appears pre-filled; `/invite?token=…` page validates the token and prefills the email on the sign-in form; base64url JWT padding fix ensures email extraction works for all token lengths; `/invite` accessible when already signed in
- **Vite polling watcher** — enabled for WSL2 HMR reliability
- **Dead code removed** — register-mode state, fields, and branches cleaned up after Sign Up was replaced

## Code review fixes (post-review commits)

- **P1**: Pad base64url JWT segment before `atob()` — without this, tokens whose payload length % 4 ≠ 0 throw and the "Request access" button never renders after Google not_invited
- **P2**: Add `/invite` route to `AuthenticatedApp` — invite links previously redirected to `/` if the user was already signed in
- **P3**: Read router location state in `AuthLanding` — "Continue to sign in" on InvitePage now actually prefills the email field

## CI and security fixes (post-review commits)

- **mypy**: Guard `cleaned_data` None before attribute access in `PieceStateAdminForm.clean()`
- **ESLint**: `InvitePage` derives initial state from `token` at render time instead of calling `setState` synchronously inside `useEffect`
- **Account enumeration**: allowlist gate fires before duplicate-email check in `auth_register` — uninvited callers probing a known email get 403, not 400
- **Token kind validation**: `verify_invite_token` checks `kind == "invite"` and raises `BadSignature` on mismatch, preventing cross-context token reuse
- **Redundant index**: `db_index=True` removed from `AllowedEmail.email` (`unique=True` already implies an index); migration 0013 drops the extra non-unique index
- **Unused import**: `from django.db import models` removed from `auth_views.py`
- **Test fixture**: `PROD = override_settings(IS_PRODUCTION=True)` moved to `conftest.py` so all test files share one canonical decorator
- **`TestAuthGoogle`**: `setup_method` creates an `AllowedEmail.APPROVED` row matching what migration 0012 does for pre-existing production users

## Production setup checklist

1. Create a Resend account and add a sending domain (`noreply@potterdoc.com`)
2. Configure DKIM/SPF via the Resend dashboard (no MX record needed for sending)
3. Set env vars: `EMAIL_HOST=smtp.resend.com`, `EMAIL_PORT=465`, `EMAIL_HOST_USER=resend`, `EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD=<api-key>`, `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL=noreply@potterdoc.com`, `INVITE_LINK_BASE_URL=https://potterdoc.com`
4. Run `migrate` — the seed migration creates `AllowedEmail` rows for all existing users
5. After verifying sign-in still works, flip Google OAuth client to production mode in Google Cloud Console

Summary

This PR fixes C-0001 so registry-less Docker Hub images are evaluated against `docker.io` entries in `untrustedRegistries`. Today the policy only checks `container.image.startsWith(registry)`, so `image: nginx` bypasses a `docker.io` deny configuration.

Fixes #90 
### Changes

- Add CEL logic that derives the image registry before matching.
- Treat images without an explicit registry host as Docker Hub.
- Treat one-segment image names as Docker Hub library images.
- Match registry boundaries with `registry + '/'` to avoid spoofed domains such as `docker.io.evil.com`.
- Apply the same helper expression to Pod, workload template, and CronJob paths.
- Add regression tests for explicit and implicit Docker Hub images plus spoofed registry names.

### Testing

```bash
cd controls/C-0001
python ../../scripts/run-control-tests.py
```

Regression cases:

```yaml
image: nginx
```

```yaml
image: library/nginx
```

```yaml
image: docker.io.evil.com/nginx
```

### Why this is safe

The change only affects how the image registry is derived before applying the configured deny list. Users who already deny `docker.io` get the behavior Kubernetes image resolution implies. The explicit registry path continues to work.

Description

This PR resolves a cache consistency issue in the upload processing workflow caused by cache validation relying only on uploaded filenames and selected language values.

Previously, processed upload state validation used:

st.session_state.get("last_processed") != f"{uploaded_file.name}_{language}"

As a result, cache reuse behavior depended solely on the uploaded file name and language selection, without considering the actual file contents.

This created a scenario where modified documents re-uploaded with the same filename could incorrectly reuse stale cached analysis results.

In particular:

File content changes were ignored during cache validation
Updated documents with unchanged filenames could bypass reprocessing workflows
Cached analysis results could become stale or inaccurate
Document analysis behavior became non-deterministic across uploads
Users could receive outdated processing results for modified files

Because the caching workflow did not uniquely identify document content versions, cache invalidation reliability depended on filename changes rather than actual file integrity.

This weakened analysis correctness guarantees and increased the risk of stale processing data being presented to users.

The updated implementation introduces content-aware cache validation using file integrity checks as part of the cache key generation workflow.

Uploaded files are now validated using content-based identifiers in addition to contextual metadata, ensuring modified documents trigger fresh analysis processing even when filenames remain unchanged.

With these changes:

Cache validation accurately reflects document content changes
Modified uploads correctly trigger re-analysis workflows
Stale cached analysis results are prevented from being reused
Cache keys uniquely identify document content versions
Document processing behavior becomes deterministic and reliable
Analysis accuracy improves for repeated uploads
Caching workflows align with content-integrity best practices

These improvements strengthen processing correctness, improve cache reliability, and reduce the risk of stale analysis results being served for updated documents.

✨ Changes Included

Replaced filename-only cache validation logic
Added file content integrity checks to cache key generation
Improved upload cache invalidation reliability
Ensured modified documents trigger fresh processing workflows
Prevented stale analysis results from being reused incorrectly
Improved determinism of upload processing behavior
Strengthened consistency of document analysis workflows

🧪 Testing Done

Verified modified files with identical filenames trigger reprocessing
Tested unchanged files correctly reuse cached analysis results
Confirmed cache validation detects document content changes
Validated accurate analysis rendering after repeated uploads
Tested upload workflows across different language selections
Checked no regressions in normal document processing behavior
Confirmed deterministic cache invalidation and re-analysis handling

closes #540 What does this PR do?

Adopts tool-side empty/whitespace identifier rejection across the destructive class of tools per the maintainer signal on #1294 (kingpanther13: belt-and-suspenders, per-tool nuance). Three failure modes are closed:

1. **Destructive intent loss** — `action = "update" if id else "create"` previously routed an empty-string `label_id` / `category_id` / area `id` / `helper_id` / `item` silently to `create` (or `update`, in the `ha_set_todo_item` case) when the caller intended the other. Now surfaces a structured `VALIDATION_INVALID_PARAMETER` error naming the offending parameter instead.

2. **Whitespace gap on partial guards** — existing `if not name` / `if not helper_id` / `if x is None` checks on `ha_config_set_helper` (simple + flow create branches), `ha_set_area_or_floor` (area + floor create branches), and `ha_manage_energy_prefs` (`stat_consumption` on add_device/remove_device) were truthy-true for `"   "` because `bool(" ") is True`. Upgraded to also reject whitespace-only strings.

3. **Misleading delete/service-call errors** — destructive remove/delete/disable/update/install tools that passed identifier parameters straight to the backend would surface as misleading HA-side "not found" or service-call errors when the identifier was empty/whitespace. Each is now guarded with a pre-flight that names the offending parameter.

A new shared helper `validate_identifier_not_empty()` in `src/ha_mcp/tools/helpers.py` centralises the empty/whitespace pre-flight check. It returns the validated value (typed `str`) so call sites can rebind to narrow `str | None → str` for mypy without a duplicate inline check, and accepts a `message` override for context-specific phrasing. `None` stays rejected by the helper — callers permitting the documented "list-all" / "create-new" sentinel gate with `if value is not None:` first.

Summary
This PR integrates **Gitleaks** into the CI/CD pipeline to automate secret scanning. This ensures that no hardcoded credentials (AWS keys, tokens, etc.) are committed to the repository, which is a critical safeguard before transitioning the repository from Private to Public.

## Changes
- Created `.gitleaks.toml`: Configuration file with a global allowlist for non-sensitive report files.
- Created `.gitleaksignore`: Initialized with historical fingerprints of known false positives (specifically the PNG header identified in PR #241).
- Updated `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: Added a `Gitleaks Scan` job pinned to a secure commit SHA (`ff98106`) for v2.3.9 of the `gitleaks-action`.
- Configured `fetch-depth: 0` in the checkout step to allow scanning of the full commit history of the branch.

## Local Validation
Extensive local testing was conducted using the Gitleaks Docker container:
1. **False Positive Check:** Verified that the current project state is "Clean" (the image resizing fix in PR #241 successfully bypasses the scanner).
2. **Detection Logic:** Confirmed detection by injecting high-confidence secret patterns (e.g., Slack Webhooks) into the worktree.
3. **Entropy Filtering:** Observed that the scanner correctly filters out low-entropy or "empty" headers to maintain a high signal-to-noise ratio in CI.

## Checklist
- [x] `ruff check .` passes
- [x] `ruff format --check .` passes
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=src mypy src/app/` passes
- [x] `pytest` passes
- [x] **No hardcoded secrets**
- [x] Commit messages follow the standard

What Changed

- Reject non-finite `/bridge/lock` amounts (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`) immediately after parsing.
- Add regression coverage proving those payloads return `400` with the existing `invalid amount` response instead of reaching base-unit conversion or min/max checks.

## Why

`float("NaN")` bypasses normal min/max comparisons and then raises during `int(round(...))`, producing an unhandled error path. Non-finite values should be treated the same as other invalid amounts before any lock state or proof handling runs.

Fixes #5361

## Summary

- **#38 (critical):** `sanitize_new_session` no longer relies on `str.startswith` for the command-path allowlist. A path like `~/.local/binEVIL/x` could previously bypass the `~/.local/bin` check. Replaced with `cmd_path == p or p in cmd_path.parents`.
- **#44:** Every `subprocess.run` in the async handlers (`new_session`, `halt`, `focus`) is now wrapped in `asyncio.to_thread`, and `halt` uses `await asyncio.sleep` instead of the blocking `time.sleep`. The event loop no longer stalls for up to 15 s during a focus or halt action.
- **#33:** `halt` now re-verifies the target PID still refers to a Claude process via `is_claude_process` before sending SIGINT. A PID-reuse race now returns 409 instead of signalling an unrelated process.
- **#47:** `log-tail` caps `?limit` to 1..500 via `Query` validation, reads at most the trailing 5 MB of the JSONL, and runs the file I/O off the event loop.
- **#55:** `actions.py` now imports `VALUE_TAKING_FLAGS` from `process_detector` rather than maintaining a drifted local copy. Flags like `--effort high` no longer spuriously return 400.
- **#35:** `focus_iterm.applescript` was unreachable since #25 made `window_id` a UUID string (the script does numeric comparison). Removed the file and the dead `elif sess.iterm_window_id and sess.iterm_tab_id` branch.

Summary

Replaces the recompute-from-cached-states approach (#69 / PR #71) with a
single-process capture pipeline that takes attention as a byproduct of the
same `model.generate()` call that produces hidden states — matching upstream
[XavierZhang2002/ICR_Probe](https://github.com/XavierZhang2002/ICR_Probe)'s
reference implementation byte-for-byte (validated by a numerical-equivalence
gate against the vendored upstream `_pre_process_attn`).

Closes #72. Supersedes PR #71 (to be closed as superseded).

**Spec:** [specs/issue_72_inference_capture_rewrite.md](specs/issue_72_inference_capture_rewrite.md)
**Paper / code resolution notes:** [notes/icr_probe_paper_notes.md](notes/icr_probe_paper_notes.md)

## What's delivered

### Capture pipeline (issue's "Concrete plan" 1–6 — done)

- **`activation_logging/generate_capture.py`** — stitching + logprob primitives
  for B=1 and B≥2 (`stitch_response_to_response`, `stitch_response_hidden_states`,
  `stitch_prompt_hidden_states`, `extract_logprobs`, plus `_batched` variants).
- **`activation_logging/inference_capture_writer.py`** — memmap-native writer
  with append-only `meta.jsonl` as the commit point. Resume semantics: on
  reopen, rebuild written-hash set from `meta.jsonl`, skip already-committed
  samples, overwrite partially-written memmap rows. Config-field validation
  on resume.
- **`scripts/capture_inference.py`** — single-process orchestrator. Loads
  HF model in `eager` attention, runs `model.generate(output_attentions=True,
  output_hidden_states=True, output_scores=True, return_dict_in_generate=True)`,
  stitches, computes ICR per layer, computes `hallucinated = not is_correct(...)`
  inline using the task module's evaluator, writes via the memmap writer.
  Supports `--batch-size {1, 4+}`, `--index-start / --index-end / --shuffle-seed`
  for deterministic appendable slicing, and `--step eval-only` for re-labeling
  without GPU.
- **`activation_research/icr_score.py`** + **`activation_research/icr_score_gpu.py`** —
  ported `compute_icr_score` from #69 Wave 4a; added a batched `(B, L)` GPU
  kernel that runs in the same forward pass when `batch_size > 1`.
- **`activation_research/icr_dataset.py`** — `ICRDataset` with `mode="memmap"`
  and `mode="memmap-raw"` that reads the new layout directly (no shim through
  the old zarr contract).
- **Numerical-equivalence gate** — `tests/test_generate_capture.py` runs our
  stream-stitched `response_attention[s, l]` against the vendored upstream
  reference on the same `model.generate()` output; asserts agreement to fp16
  tolerance. Must pass before any re-capture run.

### Dispatch infrastructure (not in original plan, but required to actually run the re-capture)

- **`scripts/dispatch/claim.py`** + **`_claim_cli.py`** — coordinator-free
  FS-claim-queue: atomic `pending/` → `claimed/<wid>/` renames over NFS,
  heartbeat-based stale-claim GC, durable `done/` / `failed/` transitions
  with `.err` sidecar.
- **`scripts/dispatch/generate_manifest.py`** — cell-JSON generator with
  CLI-configurable capture hyperparameters and `--cap N` headline-grid
  sampling (deterministic shuffle + appendable-later slices).
- **`scripts/dispatch/worker.sh`** — coordinator-free worker. Pinned to the
  p311 mamba env; HF/Transformers offline-mode forced (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`,
  `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1`); `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` redirected to bypass
  shared-MPS-daemon stalls; signal trap kills capture child and exits
  explicitly (doesn't double-fail by claiming the next cell on SIGTERM).
- **`scripts/smoketest_capture_72.sh`** — GPU smoketest, parametrized by
  `SMOKETEST_MODEL` env var.

## Storage layout

Per `(dataset, model_slug, slice)`:

```
shared/icr_capture/{dataset}[_train]_{model_slug}_{start}-{end}/
  config.json
  meta.jsonl                         # authoritative valid-rows commit log
  generation.jsonl
  eval_results.json                  # synthesized at finalize()
  response_activations.npy           # (N, L+1, S, H) fp16  memmap
  response_attention.npy             # (N, L,   R, R) fp16  memmap
  prompt_activations.npy             # (N, L+1, P, H) fp16  memmap
  prompt_token_ids.npy               # (N, P)         int32  memmap
  response_token_ids.npy             # (N, S)         int32  memmap
  response_token_logprobs.npy        # (N, S)         fp32   memmap
  response_topk_token_ids.npy        # (N, S, K)      int32  memmap
  response_topk_logprobs.npy         # (N, S, K)      fp32   memmap
  prompt_len.npy / response_len.npy  # (N,)           int32
  icr_scores.npy                     # (N, L)         fp32   np.save
```

## Resume / crash semantics

Per-sample write order is `memmap rows → generation.jsonl fsync → meta.jsonl
fsync`. `meta.jsonl` is the commit point. Crash mid-sample leaves at most one
dangling `generation.jsonl` line (ignored on resume because the hash isn't in
the `meta.jsonl` set); memmap row gets overwritten on re-process. A dead
worker's claim is reclaimed by the next `worker.sh` startup GC (cells move
back to `pending/` after the 5-minute heartbeat-staleness threshold).

- **Issue #70** (probe + trainer) will consume the new layout via the
  `ICRDataset(mode="memmap")` reader landed here.
- **Opportunistic stale-claim GC** inside `claim_next_cell` would let live

  currently the only availability gap.

## Summary

Revises the Panel conceptual contract across four docs so Panel is no longer defined only as a command-oriented checkbox executor. Panel is now described as **artifact-intent oriented**: the agent may surface likely next intentions as reviewable proposals; the user recognizes, corrects, or confirms; only confirmed intent enters governed, receipt-bearing execution.

This avoids the "Panel = checkbox executor" misunderstanding while preserving the command/receipt semantics at the execution boundary and keeping Panel, Canvas/Chat, and Automation as distinct, non-collapsible surfaces.

## Changed Docs

|------|--------|
| `docs/INTERACTION_SURFACES_AND_AUTHORITY/DEFINE_PANEL_AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY.md` | Updated one-sentence authority statement, cognitive posture section, preamble, and reviewer summary to use artifact-intent oriented framing with explicit proposal/confirmation layering. |

## Key invariants preserved

- **Panel/Canvas/Automation remain separate.** The non-collapsibility argument is now *stronger* not weaker: the Panel/Chat section explicitly states Panel is not a co-authoring surface, not a generic conversation surface, and not a Canvas Suggestion Flow variant.
- **Command/receipt semantics remain at the execution boundary.** No existing execution-path language was removed. Panel is proposal-oriented *before* confirmation and command/receipt-oriented *at* the execution boundary. Both layers coexist.
- **LLM output is not authority.** The updated docs reinforce that proposal generation is cognition/proposal/clarification class. No LLM output bypasses human confirmation for governed mutations.
- **No runtime behavior claimed beyond what is shipped.** The conceptual role section in `PANEL_AGENT.md` explicitly references PA2-FREEFORM and PA2-SUGGESTED-CHECKBOXES as the current runtime realization and does not claim new behavior.

## Summary

Adds `companion-ui/docs/CANVAS_AGENT_MVP_CONTRACT.md` — the normalized Canvas Agent MVP surface contract required by #1021. Updates `companion-ui/docs/README.md` to index the new file.

## Canvas MVP Contract Summary

Canvas Agent is the **primary reason Companion UI exists**. It requires a live-editor environment — session context, undo stack, user-presence signal, and overlay affordances — that plain Obsidian markdown cannot provide without plugin-level UI.

The contract defines:
- **Active note/artifact body** as the primary working surface; note is the canonical artifact; session transcript is subordinate provenance.
- **Session lifecycle:** `start → active → paused/interrupted → closed`.
- **User-present authority** for body co-authoring (same authority class as user keystrokes). Not a bypass of the gated-execution invariant — it recognizes user-present co-authoring as a distinct mutation class from autonomous system action.
- **Direct in-place body editing** as the default Canvas posture — not suggest-then-accept. Undo is the rollback mechanism.
- **Undo/rollback** for all assistant-applied body edits within an active session.
- **Session provenance** under `.chats/<note-slug>/`, with `type: chat-session` frontmatter. Note = artifact. Session log = provenance (intent trail, not primary record).
- **Governance-bearing escape hatch:** frontmatter classification fields, cross-note operations, note lifecycle transitions, promotions, companion notes, receipts, and system artifacts are blocked from the Canvas co-authoring path and must route through the governed execution pipeline.
- **Implementation-readiness boundaries** and **open questions** for the implementation lane (undo granularity, session recovery, conflict resolution, retention policy, escape-hatch routing, session log schema).

## How Canvas Differs from Panel

| Dimension | Canvas Agent | Panel |
|---|---|---|
| Cognitive function | Co-authoring / thinking; externalize and manipulate thought | Artifact-local intent manifestation; agent surfaces likely next action for user to confirm |
| Default posture | Direct in-place body editing; no pre-commit approval | Proposal-first; user confirms before anything changes |
| Safety mechanism | Undo + session provenance | Pre-commit confirmation + governed execution receipt |
| Primary output | Evolved note body | Confirmed intent entering governed execution |
| Scope | Currently open note body during active session | Artifact-local intent and lifecycle decisions |

Panel is first-class in Companion UI — it must not be collapsed into Canvas. Panel is defined by #995, #996, #1019.

## How Canvas Core Co-authoring Differs from Canvas Bounded Suggestion Flow

| Dimension | Canvas Core (this contract) | Canvas Bounded Suggestion Flow (#868–#874) |
|---|---|---|
| Default posture | Direct in-place body editing | Stage → preview → apply/queue/discard |
| Pre-commit approval | Not required for body edits | Required; staging is the unit of interaction |
| Use case | Flowing co-authoring of note body prose | Bounded discrete proposals; governance-bearing suggestions |

Canvas bounded suggestion flow is a valid opt-in pattern for discrete proposals and governance-bearing escape hatches — it must not be misread as the default.

Summary

- Fixes #514. New tmux-transport agents no longer need a manual Enter to unstick their first turn.
- Adopts Misha/Pulse v2's prompt-delivery pattern: bracketed paste + 300ms delay + Enter. The splash dismisses itself during the delay window, no special handling needed.
- No API credits consumed (the earlier `--print` seed approach was rejected by Brad for billing reasons — `-p` mode hits the metered credit pool, defeating the whole point of tmux transport).
- Pairs with Murzik's #517 (force_restart guard bypass pre-first-turn) to make tmux cold-start fully autonomous.

## Why this works

`tmux send-keys text Enter` delivers text + Enter as a tight keystroke sequence. When claude is mid-splash-render on cold-start, the splash transition consumes the Enter, leaving the text buffered without submission.

`tmux set-buffer + paste-buffer -p + sleep + send-keys Enter`:
- Bracketed-paste (`-p`) sequences are buffered atomically by the terminal — they don't compete with claude's splash render
- The 300ms sleep gives claude time to transition past the splash (which auto-dismisses on input focus)
- The Enter arrives after claude is chat-ready, so the prompt submits cleanly

Reference: `pulse-v2/src/daemon/session-manager.ts` (Brad pointed me at this). Misha uses the same pattern with the same 300ms delay for claude.

## Implementation

- New method: `_TmuxControl.paste_text(text, enter=True, enter_delay_ms=300)` — three-step delivery (set-buffer → paste-buffer with `-p` → optional delayed Enter)
- Changed: `_deliver_turn` now uses `paste_text` instead of `send_keys`
- `send_keys` stays in the API for utility callers
- Per-session buffer name (`pinky-<session>`) so concurrent paste_text on different sessions don't race

## Test plan

- [x] 6 new tests:
  - `test_paste_text_sets_buffer_pastes_and_sends_enter` — verifies three-call sequence + flags (-p, -d)
  - `test_paste_text_skips_enter_when_enter_false` — staging mode (no submit)
  - `test_paste_text_short_circuits_on_set_buffer_failure` — failure handling
  - `test_paste_text_short_circuits_on_paste_failure` — failure handling
  - `test_paste_text_waits_enter_delay_between_paste_and_enter` — pins the sleep that makes the splash dismiss work
  - `test_deliver_turn_uses_paste_text_not_send_keys` — integration: worker uses new path
- [x] 3 existing tests renamed + retargeted from send_keys → paste_text (clears_meta, clears_turn_done, re_arms_turn_done failure paths)
- [x] `pytest -q tests/test_tmux_session.py` → 70 passed (was 64, 6 net new)
- [x] Full suite `pytest -q` → 2101 passed
- [x] `ruff check` clean
- [ ] Post-merge: re-run Dymok cold-start validation. Expected: net-new agent bootstrap completes end-to-end with no manual Enter.

## Coordination note

PR #517 (Murzik, #516 fix) modifies non-overlapping sections of the same file (`__init__`, `_handle_turn_complete`, `force_restart`). No merge conflict expected. Recommend merging both before validating live.

## What changed from the initial draft of this PR

Initial approach was to pre-seed a transcript via `claude --print "_"` so claude resumes a (trivial) prior conversation instead of showing the splash. Brad pointed out that `-p` mode bills the API credit pool — defeats the whole subscription-billing purpose of tmux transport. Pivoted to the Pulse v2 paste-buffer pattern at his suggestion.

## Out of scope

- #513: post-spawn tmux liveness recheck — still useful as broader structural defense.
- #515: tailer never repoints from placeholder path on cold-start. Independent of this fix; needs its own investigation.
- Channel protocol via `--dangerously-load-development-channels server:outreach` (Pulse v2's primary delivery path; tmux paste-buffer is their fallback). Bigger change; this PR's scope is parity with the fallback only.

Summary
- add a shared response-format boundary helper that returns canonical JSON only after `parse_json_output` validates it
- have the non-streaming server boundary raise HTTP 422 instead of returning HTTP 200 with non-JSON `message.content` when `response_format` output is invalid
- force EOS once the JSON logits processor has already produced a complete JSON value
- keep `response_format` constraints in direct control of generation instead of hiding them behind thinking-state handling
- keep streaming `response_format` JSON/JSON-schema deltas on the assistant `content` channel when a thinking parser classifies direct JSON as reasoning
- add structured-output, constrained-decoding, and streaming content-channel tests for the hard-fail, EOS, thinking, and streaming interactions

Fixes #538.

## Local repro
The existing upstream path in `vllm_mlx/server.py` calls `parse_json_output(json_input, response_format)`. When `is_valid=False`, it logs `JSON validation failed` and then continues to return a normal `ChatCompletionResponse`.

The first focused unit repro covers the shared helper: `apply_response_format_or_error("I will reason first...", {"type": "json_object"})` raises `InvalidResponseFormatOutput`, and the server translates that into HTTP 422 at the API boundary.

A second local Runtime repro showed constrained JSON output could parse correctly but still continue until the output cap because `JSONSchemaLogitsProcessor` did not force EOS once the suffix was already complete JSON.

A third local Runtime repro showed thinking-enabled `response_format` could allow direct JSON emissions to bypass the JSON processor when the processor was wrapped behind thinking-state handling. The upstream branch had the same `_ThinkingAwareLogitsProcessor` path in both OpenAI and Anthropic preparation.

A fourth local Runtime repro showed a long streaming `response_format={"type":"json_schema"}` request on a Qwen thinking mode emitted valid JSON through the streaming reasoning channel instead of assistant content. The local certification artifact is `/opt/ai-runtime/run/qwen-response-format-streaming-certification/20260517T052855Z/summary.json`: HTTP 200, `finish_reason=stop`, JSON/schema valid, `content_length=2243`, `reasoning_length=0` after the content-channel fix.

## Upstream code path compared
- repo: `waybarrios/vllm-mlx`
- base: `main` first checked at `6d55631`; PR branch rebased onto `c2d3aec`; streaming follow-up compared against `upstream/main` at `c2d3aec4be51f3b7bc31b7b5d489ced41b1f8fbf`
- paths:
  - `vllm_mlx/server.py` non-streaming `create_chat_completion` response-format post-processing
  - `vllm_mlx/server.py` OpenAI and Anthropic response-format logits-processor attachment
  - `vllm_mlx/server.py::stream_chat_completion` reasoning-parser delta handling and streaming response-format fence stripping
  - `vllm_mlx/api/tool_calling.py` structured-output helpers
  - `vllm_mlx/constrained/json_schema_processor.py` EOS and mask handling

## Observed behavior
Invalid structured output could be returned as a successful response after only logging a warning.

A complete JSON value could remain open for more generation instead of stopping cleanly.

When thinking was explicitly enabled with `response_format`, JSON constraints could wait behind thinking-state handling and fail to own generation from the first token.

In streaming, a thinking parser could classify valid direct JSON as `reasoning_content`, leaving `delta.content` empty even though the request contract asked for `response_format` final assistant content.

## Expected behavior
If `response_format` is requested and final non-streaming output does not parse or validate, the API should fail the request instead of returning invalid content as success.

Once constrained decoding has produced a complete JSON value, EOS should be the only allowed continuation.

For `response_format`, the JSON processor should constrain generated content directly. This patch disables thinking template flags for that request path rather than wrapping the JSON processor behind thinking detection.

For streaming `response_format`, JSON/JSON-schema deltas that a reasoning parser emits as reasoning should be promoted back to assistant content unless ordinary content is already present.

Fixes [petrosa_k8s#334](https://github.com/PetroSa2/petrosa_k8s/issues/334) — organic TA signals were silently swallowed by CIO and never published to `signals.trading.*`, causing zero execution from the TA-driven path.

**Three root causes fixed:**

- **`orchestrator.py`**: In bypass mode (`NURSE_USE_LLM_REASONING=false`), `CodeEngine` ran on the real `context.regime`. If the data manager reported `CHOPPY` or `CAPITULATION` with non-low confidence (common on the testnet), every intent was hard-blocked before reaching the NATS publish path. Fix: build `engine_context` with `bypass_regime` (RANGING) before running `CodeEngine`, so policy-based regime blocks are skipped. Risk-gate hard limits (drawdown %, open order counts) are **still enforced** — they derive from `env_stats`/`risk_limits`, not from regime.
- **`context_builder.py`**: The error-path fallback `PortfolioSummary(net_directional_exposure=1.0, ...)` used the wrong field name (`gross_exposure` is required). This caused a Pydantic `ValidationError` inside the `except` block, which propagated out of `asyncio.gather`, dropping intents silently via the "Failed to build context" path.
- **`tests/unit/test_deterministic_bypass.py`**: Added a parametrized test for `CHOPPY` and `CAPITULATION` regimes in bypass mode to prevent regression.

Summary

Hook 21 (`post_label_change_wave_field_sync`) was silently a no-op on every fire. The root cause: `_ITEM_LOOKUP_QUERY` declared `$repo` and `$num` as required GraphQL variables but never referenced them in the query body. GitHub's GraphQL API rejected every call with `variableNotUsed` errors, `gh api graphql` exited non-zero, `_default_graphql_runner` returned `""`, `_lookup_item_id` returned `None`, and `check()` returned `skip_no_item` silently (that path has no `log_posttooluse_event` call) — making all 39 remaining W11 label-batch ops no-ops.

## Design Rationale

**Why server-side traversal beats Python-side project scan:**

The old query scanned `org → projectV2 → items(first: 100)` and filtered client-side by repo name and issue number. Beyond the variable declaration bug, this had two compounding problems: (1) project 2 has 785+ items — `first: 100` caps at GitHub's GraphQL ceiling per page, silently missing any issue beyond position 100; (2) the unused `$repo`/`$num` variables are wasted declaration space that caused the entire query to fail.

The new query traverses `repository(owner, name) → issue(number) → projectItems(first: 10)` — a direct server-side path that uses all declared variables (`$org`, `$repo`, `$num`) in the body. PROJECT_NUMBER filtering remains Python-side because `projectItems` has no server-side `projectNumber` filter argument; the `first: 10` ceiling is safe since issues are rarely on more than a handful of projects.

**Why the static variable-reference test catches this bug class:**

The injection-mock pattern in `FakeGraphQLRouter` bypasses real GraphQL validation — the fake routes by query substring, not by parsing the query. A test that exercises the full `check()` path with a mock runner will always pass regardless of variable declaration bugs. The new `GraphQLVariableUsageTests` class performs regex-based static analysis on the query string itself: for each declared `$var: Type!` in the operation signature, it asserts that `$var` appears at least twice in the full string (once in the signature, once or more in the body). This catches variableNotUsed at authoring time, zero network needed.

## Ontology Context

- **Hook 21** (`post_label_change_wave_field_sync.py`): PostToolUse Bash hook, registered in `post_dispatcher.py` line 63 (runs LAST in the Bash chain after `annunaki_monitor` → `auto_add_issue_to_board` → `post_wave_kickoff_comment`). Fires on `gh issue edit --add-label / --remove-label` commands with canonical wave labels.
- **post_dispatcher.py**: Routes PostToolUse Bash events to registered hook modules.
- **Project 2** ("Cross-Repo Wave Plan"): GitHub ProjectV2 board; Wave field is a single-select field. Hook 21 syncs this field on label-edit events.
- **Companion Hook 13** (`auto_add_issue_to_board.py`): Covers the CREATE surface; Hook 21 covers the EDIT surface. Both are required for complete Wave-field invariant coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Actionable (this PR closes)
- [ ] `_ITEM_LOOKUP_QUERY` uses all declared variables (`$org`, `$repo`, `$num`) in the query body — no `variableNotUsed` errors from GitHub GraphQL
- [ ] `GraphQLVariableUsageTests` passes and catches the variableNotUsed class for all 4 query/mutation strings
- [ ] All 36 existing tests pass (0 regressions)
- [ ] Hook 21 fires successfully against a real production-shape command (confirmed via 4 manual compensations that used the same verified query shape: deploy#284, data-acquisition#52, deploy#11, main#448)

### Informational (not in this PR)
- Hook 13 (`auto_add_issue_to_board`) also doesn't set the Wave field on `gh issue create` — separate follow-up to file post-merge
- `skip_no_item` path (lines 540-547) has no `log_posttooluse_event` call — deferred decision on whether silent skip is the right shape
- Integration test variant (b) — real `gh api graphql` call against a test project — deferred for follow-up

## Out of Scope

- Hook 13 Wave-field gap on create events
- Annunaki logging of `skip_no_item` / `skip_no_auth_scope` paths
- Integration test variant using live GraphQL endpoint
- Pagination of `projectItems` beyond `first: 10` (issues are rarely on >10 projects; `first: 10` is safe in practice)

Summary

Routes the seven remaining surface-side mutation paths through the shared
`ArchiveMutationsMixin` contract introduced in #1109, completing the
cross-surface centralization tracked by #862. Adds typed result models
(`MetadataMutationResult`, `DeleteConversationResult`,
`BulkTagMutationResult`) and a single source of truth for metadata key
validation.

## Problem

Audit of master left seven divergences where CLI, MCP, and daemon
surfaces still bypassed the operation mixin:

1. `polylogue/cli/query_actions.py::apply_modifiers` set metadata via
   `repo.update_metadata` directly, skipping the conversation-existence
   check.
2. `polylogue/mcp/server_mutation_tools.py::bulk_tag_conversations`
   called `tag_store.bulk_add_tags` directly with inline 100/20 batch
   caps duplicated outside the operation layer.
3. `polylogue/mcp/server_mutation_tools.py::delete_metadata` called
   `tag_store.delete_metadata` directly with no resolution through
   the facade.
4. `polylogue/mcp/server_mutation_tools.py::delete_conversation`
   mapped `bool -> "deleted"/"not_found"` inside the surface; nothing
   guaranteed every adapter would do that the same way.
5. `polylogue/cli/query_actions.py::delete_conversations` called
   `repo.delete_conversation` directly without facade resolution or
   idempotency contract.
6. Metadata key validation (empty/whitespace, 200-char limit) was
   inline in MCP `set_metadata` only — every other surface relied on
   storage-layer behavior.
7. `polylogue/daemon/http.py::_handle_reset` had a latent async bug:
   the synchronous `_do_reset` callback called the async
   `poly.delete_conversation` and returned the coroutine into a JSON
   encode path, never deleting anything.

## Solution

- **`polylogue/operations/mutations.py`**: extended `ArchiveMutationsMixin`
  with resolve-aware typed-result entrypoints — `set_metadata_validated`,
  `delete_metadata_validated`, `delete_conversation_safe`,
  `bulk_tag_conversations` — plus the centralized
  `_validate_metadata_key` helper and a `MetadataKeyValidationError`
  exception. The previous bool-returning methods stay as low-level
  delegates.
- **`polylogue/surfaces/payloads.py`**: added typed
  `MetadataMutationResult`, `DeleteConversationResult`,
  `BulkTagMutationResult`, and `validate_metadata_key` /
  `METADATA_KEY_MAX_LENGTH` constants.
- **`polylogue/api/archive.py`**: `Polylogue.delete_conversation`,
  `update_metadata`, the new `set_metadata`, `delete_metadata`,
  `delete_conversation_safe`, and `bulk_tag_conversations` all route
  through the mixin.
- **`polylogue/cli/query_actions.py`**: `apply_modifiers` metadata writes
  go through `env.polylogue.set_metadata`; `delete_conversations` calls
  `env.polylogue.delete_conversation_safe`. Custom-repo escape hatches
  preserved for test/batch tools.
- **`polylogue/mcp/server_mutation_tools.py`**: bulk tagging, set/delete
  metadata, and delete-conversation tools route through the facade and
  the typed results; key validation runs at the surface boundary before
  opening the facade so unit tests can exercise the rejection path
  without standing up an archive.
- **`polylogue/daemon/http.py`**: `_handle_reset` now awaits
  `delete_conversation_safe` through the existing `_sync_run` async
  bridge and removes the obsolete `_get_or_create_polylogue` helper.
- **`tests/unit/operations/test_mutations.py`** (new): 17 tests covering
  every (mutation, exists/missing, validation) pair on top of a real
  SQLite archive built via `ConversationBuilder`.
- **`tests/unit/mcp/test_tool_contracts.py`**, **`tests/infra/mcp.py`**:
  refreshed mocks to track the new facade-typed return values.
- **`tests/property/test_filter_chain_laws.py`**: fix for an inherited
  property-test failure (provider filter replaces prior provider rather
  than intersecting, so the monotonicity law required tightening to
  an impossible provider on disagreement). Surfaced by `devtools verify`
  before this PR could be merged.

## Summary

- DCR endpoint `POST /api/v1/oauth/register` now omits `client_secret` (and `plaintext_secret`) from the response for public clients, restoring RFC 7591 §3.2.1 compliance and unblocking Claude Code / ChatGPT / Cursor MCP OAuth flows that previously failed with `Existing OAuth client information is required when exchanging an authorization code` → `invalid_client 401` on `/token`.
- Server side, the secret is no longer generated/hashed/encrypted: `client_secret_hash=""` sentinel (authlib short-circuits the secret check on the `"none"` branch — kagura-memory `19adf25b`); `plaintext_secret_encrypted=None`; `visibility_expires_at=None`.
- Admin and regenerate endpoints unchanged (still issue real secrets per confidential-client contract). Forward-only fix — existing prod DCR rows keep their real hashes; cached old clients get the same 401 they get today and re-register naturally.

## Implementation notes

- **Schema**: `OAuth2ClientWithSecretResponse.client_secret` widened to `str | None = None`. Backward-compatible (admin/regenerate still pass real strings; widening is permissive).
- **Decorator**: `/register` gains `response_model_exclude={"client_secret","plaintext_secret"}` so the fields are *absent* from JSON, not just `null`. Alternatives considered and rejected:
  - `response_model_exclude_none=True` — also drops legit-None fields like `owner_id`, breaks existing test assertions.
  - Custom `JSONResponse` — bypasses response_model validation contract.
  - Returning `null` — some OAuth client libs treat empty-secret Basic Auth as in-scope, would re-trigger the bug.
- **Tests**: existing `test_accepted_returns_201` strengthened with negative assertions on response/DB state + `fake_encryptor.encrypt.assert_not_called()` (mutation-style — proves the encryption code path is unreachable). NEW integration test `test_dcr_token_exchange_with_pkce_only_returns_200` pins the full DCR → auth-code → `/token` (PKCE-only, no Basic Auth) → 200 round-trip. PKCE S256 reuses `authlib.oauth2.rfc7636.create_s256_code_challenge` for prod-parity. Fixture teardown extended to clean orphan `oauth_authorization_codes` rows.

## Summary

Batches three related backend-hardening issues into one cohesive PR. All three touch `backend/routes/vault_routes.py` + `backend/storage/resume_vault.py`; doing them as separate PRs would have caused back-to-back merge conflicts.

### #34 — Authentication + CORS
Vault endpoints were fully unauthenticated with wildcard CORS. Added:
- `before_request` handler on `vault_bp` requiring `Authorization: Bearer <API_SECRET>` (matches the existing pattern in `routes/admin_routes.py`)
- **Timing-safe** comparison via `secrets.compare_digest()` (not `==`)
- **Case-insensitive Bearer** scheme parsing: `re.compile(r"^Bearer\s+(\S+)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE)`
- `.strip()` on `API_SECRET` env var (defends against `.env`-file trailing whitespace)
- `OPTIONS` requests bypassed (CORS preflight must succeed)
- Dev passthrough when `API_SECRET` is unset, with startup warning
- Auth-failure logging at WARNING level (IP + path, token NOT logged)
- CORS allowlist via `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var (comma-separated). When set, only allowlisted origins get echoed. `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is emitted **only** when a specific allowlisted origin is echoed (never with `*` — that combination is browser-rejected per CORS spec)

### #35 — Path traversal in `canonical_filename`
`company.replace(" ", "_")` was the only sanitization. Adversarial input like `company = "../../etc/passwd"` could escape the vault directory. Added:
- Regex `[^A-Za-z0-9_-]` strips dots, slashes, backslashes, null bytes, Unicode in one pass
- Empty-after-sanitization → `ValueError` → 400
- `os.path.realpath` assertion in `save_pdf_to_vault` against `VAULT_DIR` realpath (defense in depth — catches symlink shenanigans)
- Route-layer 80-char cap on `company` and `role`

### #36 — PDF magic-byte + size validation
`save_pdf_to_vault` previously wrote arbitrary bytes to disk. Added:
- `pdf_bytes.startswith(b"%PDF-")` magic-byte check at storage layer
- `len(pdf_bytes) <= 10_000_000` (10 MB) cap; rejects with 413
- Cheap-first ordering: size check before magic before realpath
- Frontend keeps its existing 5 MB cap as defense-in-depth (faster UX feedback)

### Frontend changes (`App.jsx`)
Added auth-token helpers:
```js
const apiToken = () => { ... reads localStorage["vault_token"] ... };
const authHeaders = () => apiToken() ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiToken()}` } : {};
```
Spread `...authHeaders()` into all 7 vault `fetch` callsites (and only vault — non-vault fetches untouched). Returns `{}` when no token is set, so dev with unset `API_SECRET` continues to work transparently.

## Multi-agent workflow

- **Round 1** (2 parallel implementation agents — Agent B picked on test coverage: 21 vs 17 cases)
- **5 critic lenses**: correctness, security, tests, API/integration, code quality
- **Round 1 verdicts**: 1 ✅, 2 ⚠️, **2 ❌ REJECTED** — security and API/integration found real blockers:
  - Timing-unsafe `==` comparison (security)
  - `Allow-Credentials: true` + `Allow-Origin: *` = browser-rejected (security + correctness + API)
  - Fragile `.replace("Bearer ", "")` parsing (security + correctness)
  - Auth failure logging missing
  - Frontend would 401 every vault call in production — no `Authorization` header (API)
- **Round 2**: applied all 6 must-fix items
- **Re-critique by all 5 lenses**: **5/5 ✅ APPROVED** — full consensus

## Test coverage

`backend/tests/test_vault_routes.py` — 29 tests across:

**Auth (10)**: missing header, wrong Bearer, correct Bearer, dev passthrough, OPTIONS bypass, wrong scheme (`Basic xyz`), lowercase `bearer foo`, uppercase `BEARER foo`, empty token, env-var whitespace stripping

**CORS (5)**: default `*`, allowlist match, allowlist mismatch, `Allow-Credentials` present only with allowlist, `Allow-Credentials` absent with `*`

**Path traversal (6)**: `canonical_filename` sanitize, role-empty 400, route 80-char caps, traversal company sanitization, realpath monkeypatch escape, multi-component sanitization

**PDF validation (8)**: route non-PDF 400, route oversize 413, route valid 200, storage non-PDF, storage oversize, storage valid roundtrip, exact-10MB-boundary accepted, exact-byte-over-limit rejected

Full backend suite: **127/127 passed in 45.02s**

Frontend build: **646.28 kB / 180.60 kB gzip** — unchanged (token helpers compress to noise).

## Migration / deployment notes

1. **Setting `API_SECRET` is opt-in.** Leaving it unset preserves current behavior (no auth required). On Render: add `API_SECRET=<random>` to the env vars when you're ready to gate.
2. **For browser callers after enabling auth**: open DevTools console and run `localStorage.setItem("vault_token", "<your API_SECRET value>")`. The vault UI will then send the header automatically. A proper login UI is tracked as **#46**.
3. **CORS allowlist** is also opt-in via `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Recommend setting to `https://narendranathe.github.io` (or wherever GitHub Pages serves the dashboard) when enabling auth.

- **#41** — unbounded `job_description` is the real DoS lever (TF-IDF over 95 docs runs regardless of `top_n`)

What's the Problem?

RAG systems are vulnerable to:
- **Prompt Injection Attacks**: Users can trick the system into ignoring safety rules
- **SQL/Command Injection**: Attackers can run malicious queries
- **Jailbreak Attempts**: Users can bypass security restrictions
- **Citation Issues**: Sources might be missing, duplicated, or incorrect
- **Information Leakage**: Sensitive data could be exposed in responses

## What's Fixed?

Complete security layer for RAG with 2 main components:

### 1. Prompt Injection Defense
Detects and blocks malicious queries before they reach the RAG system.

**Files:**
- `rag/safety.py` 

**Features:**
- Detects injection keywords (ignore instructions, role-play, etc.)
- Detects SQL injection patterns ('1'='1', UNION SELECT, etc.)
- Detects command injection (shell commands, file operations)
- Detects jailbreak attempts
- Classifies threat levels (SAFE, WARNING, CRITICAL)
- Query validation (length, format, safety checks)
- Response validation (checks for sensitive data leaks)
- Domain scoping (keeps queries agricultural-focused)
- Query sanitization (removes dangerous patterns)

**API Safety Levels:**
- SAFE: Legitimate agricultural questions
- WARNING: Suspicious patterns detected
- CRITICAL: Injection/jailbreak/exfiltration attempt

### 2. Citation Integrity
Ensures all responses are properly cited and sources are valid.

**Files:**
- `rag/citation_manager.py` 

**Features:**
- Citation objects with source tracking
- Citation contexts for managing response sources
- Automatic duplicate detection
- Low-confidence citation detection
- Circular reference detection
- Citation coverage scoring
- Format citations as Markdown/JSON/HTML
- Integrity validation (confidence, completeness, sources)

closes #680

Summary

- CRITICAL security fix: `ProtectedDataFlow` write-protection (`enable_read_only_mode`, `production_safe`, `add_model_protection`, `add_field_protection`) was a facade orphan — `WriteProtectionEngine.check_operation` had zero async-reachable production call sites, so every protected write **silently succeeded** on `db.express.*` and `runtime.execute(workflow.build())`. Operators who enabled read-only protection believed writes were blocked; they were not.
- **Shard 1a** (`e876700d7`): re-base `ProtectionViolation` on `NodeExecutionError` so a blocked write propagates typed through `AsyncNode.execute_async`'s exception re-wrap on the workflow-runtime path (would otherwise surface as a generic `NodeExecutionError`). Blast radius audited clean (2 independent agents): zero `except NodeExecutionError` site swallows it.
- **Shard 1b** (`c27528938`): add `async def async_run` enforcement override in `protect_dataflow_node()`; delete the dead sync `run()` override (closes the I1 double-check vector); restore the 2 `# KNOWN COVERAGE GAP — tracked: issue #1050` tests to assert end-to-end runtime enforcement (same commit, orphan-detection Rule 4a). Also fixes a latent I7 bug surfaced by the wiring: `count` was mis-mapped and spuriously blocked under read-only — now correctly `OperationType.READ`.
- `97d198d4f`: correct a pyright suppression code (warning was unsilenced). `0ce4c597f`: spec §4 present-tense conformance per specs-authority §5.

Contract + invariants I1–I9: `specs/dataflow-protection.md`. Root-cause + design + red-team convergence: `workspaces/issue-1050-protection-orphan-async/`.

## Behavior change (see CHANGELOG)

Writes that previously slipped through only because protection was a no-op will now correctly raise `ProtectionViolation`. Operators relying on the broken no-op state MUST review their protection configs before upgrading. `ProtectionViolation` is now a `NodeExecutionError` subclass (downstream `except NodeExecutionError` now also catches it). No deprecation shim — a fake safety gate made real is not a removal (zero-tolerance Rule 2).

Adds `gh-post reply-inline OWNER/REPO PR < replies.jsonl` — a batched JSONL stream for Copilot inline review replies. This is the single most frequent body-passing pattern in the wrapped surface that v0 intentionally deferred.

Each reply runs through the existing hardwrap validator stack before any send, so the silent-bypass class that motivated the wrapper is now closed for this endpoint too.

Closes #1.

## Changes

- `gh_post.py` — `cmd_reply_inline`, helpers `_validate_repo_slug` and `_parse_reply_entries`, one new dispatch branch in `main()` ahead of the existing `SPECS` lookup; `_emit_subprocess_output` extracted so `cmd_post` and `cmd_reply_inline` share newline-normalized stdout / stderr forwarding

## Impact

Additive only.
`SPECS` is unchanged.
The existing argv guards (`_reject_inline_body`, `_reject_body_authoring_flags`)

The `_emit_subprocess_output` extraction touches `cmd_post`'s body in a behavior-preserving way (verified by `test_cmd_post_forwards_via_emit_helper` and the pre-existing end-to-end tests).

Summary

Closes #9

Add optional per-tenant ceilings on **vCPU**, **memory**, and **data disk size**. When enabled, ``create_tenant`` rejects requests above any configured limit with a clear 400 error.

Disabled by default — fully backward compatible.

## Config

```yaml
# config.yml
quotas:
  enabled: false                  # default off, opt-in
  max_vcpu_per_tenant: 4
  max_mem_mb_per_tenant: 8192
  max_data_disk_mb: 16384
```

Each limit is independent; setting any to ``0`` disables that dimension only.

## Behavior

| State | Effect |
|---|---|
| ``quotas.enabled: false`` (default) | No checks — backward compat |
| ``quotas.enabled: true`` | ``create_tenant`` validates against each limit; rejects with 400 + error explaining the limit |

Validation rules:
- Limit is **inclusive** at the boundary (``vcpu == max`` → allowed)
- One-over-max rejected (``vcpu == max + 1`` → 400)
- Validation runs **before** ``restore_from`` lookup — even backup restores are guarded
- Error message includes the actual configured limit so callers can retry

## Out of scope (future)

- ``max_tenants_per_key`` (requires DDB GSI by ``api_key_id``, deferred)
- ``network_bandwidth_mbps`` (would require host-side ``tc`` on TAP devices)

## Summary

- **The pain**: PR #89 made `on_success: delete` the default, so every run starts cold: image pull (~2–5 min for 12 GB pytorch images), `setup:` re-runs, full rsync of the staging payload. Across a 100-job sweep that's *hours* of wall-time per sweep paid for at GPU rate.
- **The fix**: a fourth lifecycle action `recycle`. Pauses the pod at end-of-run AND preserves the state-file. The next `runpod-deploy run` with the same `state_file:` resumes the paused pod (via `runpodctl pod start`) instead of provisioning a fresh one. Image pull + cold-boot skipped — typically 3–5 min saved per recurring run.
- **The escape hatches**: drift detection (image / GPU / datacenter mismatch) falls through to fresh-create with a WARNING. `runpod-deploy run --force-fresh` bypasses resume for one invocation. `on_failure: recycle` is rejected at validation (failed pods may have corrupted state).

Closes #90.

## Design (locked via `/exploring-options`)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Resume-lookup mechanism | **State-file pointer.** No new YAML; reuses existing `state_file:` field. |
| Drift detection scope | **Image + GPU + datacenter.** Mismatch → log WARNING, delete stale, fresh-create. |
| `on_failure: recycle` | **Rejected at validation** — recycle is success-path only. |
| CLI override | **`--force-fresh`** flag mirrors the existing override taxonomy. |
| State-file payload | Extended from `{pod_id, gpu_id}` to `{pod_id, gpu_id, image, datacenter_id}` for drift detection. Older state-files (missing the new fields) treated as drift. |

## What's NOT in this PR (deliberately deferred)

- **Tagging paused pods with provenance** (e.g., recording whether a pod was paused via `on_failure: stop` vs `on_success: recycle`). Considered but rejected as overengineering for v1. ## Authority hierarchy

The fully automatic G0-G8 semantic classifier is not validated. The frozen
authority hierarchy is:

```text
TPTM G0-G8 -> deterministic evidence extractor
G0/G1 -> authorized automatic mechanical exclusion
G2-G8 -> deterministic evidence extraction only
structured Q1-Q10 review -> bounded semantic screening authority
executable family validation -> final scientific admission authority
```

The validated release is commit
`f7814ec65392abf6e5b8a330ca6d6dc70637e094`, tree
`f298bf399846b60db574566030c50e7978a3b59b`. Its G0-G8 semantics, rules,
configuration, supported languages, Q1-Q10 form, sampling policy, and exact
focal-hypothesis disagreement policy are unchanged.

## Queue and predecessor history

This successor reuses the exact v0.1.19 sealed queue. It never regenerates,
shuffles, samples, filters, or re-ranks it. The queue contains 7,565 candidates
from 3,506 repositories. Its file, manifest, and input identity-set SHA-256
values are frozen in `protocol.json` and the freeze manifest.

The v0.1.19 pilot remains immutable history. Positions 1 and 2 were opened and
terminally rejected as `REJECT_NOT_TRUST_BOUNDARY_RELEVANT`; no final, reserve,
or provisional family resulted. Those decisions have no v0.2.0 decision
authority.

The successor starts logically at position 1. Position 1 must be processed
before position 2, and position 2 before position 3. Reprocessing positions 1
and 2 does not increment global unique-opened-anchor accounting. Old Stage-1
semantic decisions are not inputs to successor review.

At initialization:

```text

historical_unique_opened_anchors=2
global_unique_opened_anchors=2
next_due_position=1
FINAL=0
RESERVE_REQUIRED=0
FINAL_TARGET=6
trust_categories_represented=0
global_action=CONTINUE
```

## Hybrid routing

The only routes are:

```text
authorized G0/G1 mechanical exclusion -> AUTO_MECHANICAL_REJECT
complete feasible G2-G8 evidence -> AUTO_RETAIN_FOR_CONSTRUCTION
other supported G2-G8 state -> STRUCTURED_REVIEW_REQUIRED
unsupported required language -> OUT_OF_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED
true analyzer or integrity failure -> ANALYSIS_ERROR
```

No G2-G8 semantic negative may become a terminal rejection without structured
review. `AUTO_RETAIN_FOR_CONSTRUCTION` authorizes constrained construction; it
does not admit a final family.

## Structured review

Reviewer A performs the first review for every
`STRUCTURED_REVIEW_REQUIRED` case. Reviewer B is blind to Reviewer A's decision
and independently reviews every retain, every unresolved case that may become
retain, every enriched reject under the frozen G6/G7/G8 policy, and the frozen
20% SHA-256 sample of remaining rejects. Production has no gold labels.

Every Q1-Q10 answer is `YES`, `NO`, or `UNKNOWN`. Every `YES` and `NO` cites
packet evidence. All `YES` yields `REVIEW_RETAIN`; an evidenced `NO` yields
`REVIEW_REJECT`; otherwise an `UNKNOWN` yields `REVIEW_UNRESOLVED`. There is no
confidence score, weighted vote, or free-form override.

Disagreement on the required semantic decision or exact focal hypothesis
yields `REVIEW_UNRESOLVED`. Neither reviewer is selected and no majority vote
is taken. A supported unresolved candidate with credible evidence proceeds to
`CONSTRAINED_FAMILY_FEASIBILITY_INVESTIGATION`; unresolved is neither final nor
rejected. A retain proceeds to `CONSTRAINED_FAMILY_CONSTRUCTION`; retain is not
final.

## Family construction and admission

Construction may implement `S`, `C`, `I`, `P_reuse`, `P_safe`, `F`, and `W`
inside the frozen FamilyRecipe envelope. It may not silently change predicate
type, focal transition, witness type, protected effect, construction envelope,
required category, or required F/W invariants. A necessary semantic recipe
change is a construction failure or unresolved review, never an adapted
success.

Final admission requires all of:

```text
p*(S)=TRUE
p*(C)=TRUE
p*(I)=FALSE
F(P_reuse)=PASS
W(P_reuse)=TRIGGERED
F(P_safe)=PASS
W(P_safe)=BLOCKED
exactly one isolated focal trust change
known trust category
repository-independence constraints satisfied
```

No human or Codex override can admit a family that fails an executable
invariant.

## Six-family stopping rule

Stopping is yield-driven, not a fixed candidate count:

```text
TARGET_FINAL_FAMILIES=6
REQUIRED_RESERVE_FAMILIES=0
MINIMUM_TRUST_CATEGORIES=4
MAX_FINAL_FAMILIES_PER_CATEGORY=2
MAX_OTHER_PREDECLARED=1
MAX_GLOBAL_UNIQUE_OPENED_ANCHORS=1000
```

Only `ADMIT_FINAL` increments the target. There is at most one final per
repository-independence group. Reviewer-time projections are advisory and do
not affect stopping.

## Append-only publication

Every processed position receives a durable record conforming to
`production-record.schema.json`. Candidate semantic records exclude
operational timing from their semantic hash. Review decisions, family recipe,
construction, executable validation, admission, repository group, category,
and the chain-derived stopping state remain explicit; no candidate is silently
discarded.

## Freeze boundary

The freeze task creates no candidate record, credential, or candidate-scoped
authorization and executes no screening. Candidate #3's mapping, repository,
issue or PR, source, evidence, and authorization remain unopened. The next
separate task may process only position 1.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ReviewEvidenceIndexEntry:
    evidence_id: str
    record_type: str
    stage: str
    path: str | None
    snapshot: str | None
    start_byte: int | None
    end_byte: int | None
    start_line: int | None
    end_line: int | None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.evidence_id or not self.record_type or not self.stage:
            raise ValueError("review evidence index identity fields must be non-empty")
        if self.path is not None:
            path = PurePosixPath(self.path)
            if (
                path.is_absolute()
                or "\" in self.path
                or path.as_posix() != self.path
                or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in path.parts)
            ):
                raise ValueError("review evidence paths must be canonical and relative")
        if (self.start_byte is None) != (self.end_byte is None):
            raise ValueError("review byte spans must be wholly present or absent")
        if (self.start_line is None) != (self.end_line is None):
            raise ValueError("review line spans must be wholly present or absent")
        if self.start_byte is not None and (
            self.start_byte < 0 or self.end_byte < self.start_byte  # type: ignore[operator]
        ):
            raise ValueError("review byte span is invalid")
        if self.start_line is not None and (
            self.start_line < 1 or self.end_line < self.start_line  # type: ignore[operator]
        ):
            raise ValueError("review line span is invalid")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ReviewPacket:
    schema_version: str
    protocol_id: str
    review_packet_sha256: str | None
    routing: HybridRoutingDecision
    candidate_result: CandidateResult
    review_questions: tuple[ReviewQuestionDefinition, ...]
    evidence_index: tuple[ReviewEvidenceIndexEntry, ...]
    exact_code_spans: tuple[SourceSpanEvidence, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.schema_version != REVIEW_PACKET_SCHEMA_VERSION:
            raise ValueError("review packet schema version is unsupported")
        if self.protocol_id != HYBRID_PROTOCOL_ID:
            raise ValueError("review packet protocol identity is unsupported")
        if self.review_packet_sha256 is not None and _SHA256.fullmatch(
            self.review_packet_sha256
        ) is None:
            raise ValueError("review_packet_sha256 must be a lowercase SHA-256")
        if self.routing.state not in _REVIEW_PACKET_ELIGIBLE_STATES:
            raise ValueError(
                "review packets are only valid for automatic-retain or "
                "structured-review routes"
            )
        if (
            self.routing.candidate_id != self.candidate_result.candidate_id
            or self.routing.queue_position != self.candidate_result.queue_position
        ):
            raise ValueError("review packet routing identity is inconsistent")
        if self.review_questions != REVIEW_QUESTIONS:
            raise ValueError("review packet questions must use the frozen Q1-Q10 form")
        evidence_ids = tuple(item.evidence_id for item in self.evidence_index)
        if evidence_ids != tuple(sorted(evidence_ids)) or len(set(evidence_ids)) != len(
            evidence_ids
        ):
            raise ValueError("review evidence index must be unique and ordered")
        span_ids = tuple(item.evidence_id for item in self.exact_code_spans)
        if span_ids != tuple(sorted(span_ids)) or len(set(span_ids)) != len(span_ids):
            raise ValueError("exact code spans must be unique and ordered")
        if not set(span_ids) <= set(evidence_ids):
            raise ValueError("exact code spans must resolve in the evidence index")
